guide.summary: Linear documents OAuth2 as the recommended method for applications used by others, and its default read scope covers the requested read-only issue title access for each connected user account. The documented read scope is broad account-level read access rather than issue-specific, and no write scopes are needed for the confirmed read-only request. Provider review, marketplace listing and customer-admin approval were not found in the supplied snapshots.
guide.recommendation: The requested access is documented. Follow the saved setup steps and run each representative API test; execution has not been verified.

findings.title: OAuth2 is documented for apps used by other customers
findings.detail: Linear states OAuth2 is recommended for applications that integrate with Linear, and the GraphQL docs recommend OAuth2 for applications built for others. Each customer account would connect through OAuth and pass the resulting Bearer access token to the GraphQL endpoint.
findings.appliesWhen: Each individual customer account connects through OAuth, as confirmed.

evidence.quote: Linear supports OAuth2 authentication, which is recommended if you’re building applications to integrate with Linear.
### OAuth If you’re building an application for others to use, we recommend you use OAuth2 authentication. Once you complete the authentication flow and acquire an access token, pass it

findings.title: Use the default read scope for account-level issue reads
findings.detail: The read scope gives read access for the user's account and is always present by default. It is not documented as limited to issues, so the boundary is the connected user's account visibility, which is broader than issue titles alone. No write scope is requested, which fits the read-only confirmed request.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the read-issue-titles action for each connected customer account.

evidence.quote: * `read` - (Default) Read access for the user's account. This scope will always be present.

findings.title: Create a dedicated workspace to manage the OAuth application
findings.detail: Linear recommends creating a workspace to manage the OAuth2 application because each admin user in that workspace will have access to it. This is a setup consideration for the developer, not a customer approval step.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies when the developer registers the OAuth2 application.

evidence.quote: > [!NOTE] > It is **highly recommended** you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application, as each admin user will have access.

steps.title: Register the Linear OAuth application in a dedicated management workspace
steps.detail: The developer registers the OAuth2 application in Linear and records the client_id and client_secret. steps.doneWhen: The developer has a registered OAuth application with a redirect URL and a stored client secret, and only admins who need access belong to the management workspace.

steps.title: Prepare the read-only OAuth authorization request for each customer account
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL with response_type=code, the registered client_id and redirect_uri, a random state value, and scope=read only. Do not add write scopes such as write, issues:create or comments:create. Add PKCE parameters if the developer uses them. This step only prepares the URL; it does not obtain consent.
steps.doneWhen: The authorization URL in code uses scope=read only, includes state, and points to Linear's documented authorize endpoint. No consent has been granted by this step.

evidence.quote: ### Example ```http GET https://linear.app/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URL&state=SECURE_RANDOM&scope=read HTTP/1.1
* `read` - (Default) Read access for the user's account. This scope will always be present.
`state` | (optional, **recommended**) Prevents CSRF attacks and should always be supplied. Read more about it here.

fields: client_id: from registered OAuth application
redirect_uri: developer-chosen callback URL
state: developer-generated random value
scope: read

steps.title: Each customer account connects through OAuth and returns an access token
steps.detail: Each individual customer account opens the consent URL, signs in, and approves the read scope. The developer then exchanges the returned code using a documented OAuth token method (HTTP basic authentication or client_id and client_secret parameters). The resulting Bearer access token is stored for that account only. The token endpoint path is not in the supplied snapshots and must not be guessed.
steps.doneWhen: Each tested customer account has a Bearer access token issued through its own consent, with token_type Bearer and expires_in present in the response. No token is shared across accounts.

steps.title: Read the first page of issue titles with the customer's access token
steps.detail: Send a POST to https://api.linear.app/graphql with the customer's OAuth Bearer token in the Authorization header, using only a read query: issues(first: 10, after: null) returning nodes with id and title plus pageInfo with hasNextPage and endCursor. Save hasNextPage and endCursor for the continuation step. Boundary check: this query is read-only and relies on the default read scope, which covers the user's whole account and is broader than issue titles; no write scope is requested. If a read is denied and not documented, inspect the granted scopes and the outgoing request log rather than testing writes or claiming a narrower scope.
steps.doneWhen: The response contains issues.nodes with id and title strings and an issues.pageInfo object, and hasNextPage and endCursor are saved. Nothing is created, updated or deleted.

evidence.quote: # Pagination All list responses from queries return paginated results. We implement Relay style cursor-based pagination model with `first`/`after` and `last`/`before` pagination arguments. For example, this is how to query
* `read` - (Default) Read access for the user's account. This scope will always be present.
-H 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' \

request.example: curl 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-X' 'POST' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query IssueTitles($first: Int!, $after: String) { issues(first: $first, after: $after) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }","variables":{"first":10,"after":null}}'

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: Bearer token from the authorization step
first: 10
after: null for the first page

steps.title: Continue issue title pagination until hasNextPage is false
steps.detail: Repeat the same read-only POST to https://api.linear.app/graphql with first set to 10 and after set to the previous response's issues.pageInfo.endCursor. Keep requesting while issues.pageInfo.hasNextPage is true and collect nodes from every page. Stop only when hasNextPage is false, which is the documented end of the listing; two pages are not a complete listing. Archived issues are hidden by default and are not included here. Boundary check: use the same read-only query with the same customer's OAuth Bearer token; no mutation or write scope is tested. If a read is denied and not documented, inspect the granted scopes and the request log.
steps.doneWhen: Requests continue with each returned endCursor until hasNextPage is false. Every page's nodes are collected with the same query and first value, and no page is skipped.

evidence.quote: } ``` To query the next 10, simply pass the value of `pageInfo.endCursor` as `after` parameter for the next request. You can do this as long as `pageInfo.hasNextPage` return true
and you'll paginate through all the values in the collection.
#### Archived resources Archived resources are hidden by default from the paginated responses. They can be included by passing optional `includeArchived: true` as a query parameter for pagination.

request.example: curl 'https://api.linear.app/graphql' '-X' 'POST' '-H' 'Content-Type: application/json' '-H' 'Authorization: Bearer <ACCESS_TOKEN>' '--data' '{"query":"query IssueTitles($first: Int!, $after: String) { issues(first: $first, after: $after) { nodes { id title } pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } } }","variables":{"first":10,"after":"<END_CURSOR>"}}'

fields: END_CURSOR: issues.pageInfo.endCursor from the previous response
first: 10, unchanged from the first page
ACCESS_TOKEN: the customer's OAuth Bearer token from the authorization step
